notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen last game. Trevor Zegras takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. David Jiříček is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Seeler and York.
Owen Tippett is out (lower-body injury) and missed their last game.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 43% of the team’s power-play time in 11 games, up from 2% last season.
Chris Tanev is out (lower-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Nick Blankenburg is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 15 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 76:24 together, about what it had with Blankenburg (48%).
Jack Roslovic is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Nick Paul has taken his spot beside Auston Matthews and Easton Cowan.
Kirill Marchenko returned in their last game after missing 12 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Aatu Räty was added to the roster on Nov 23 and has played beside William Nylander and Dakota Joshua.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 26 games, up from 6% last season.

story.head: Benoit returns to Toronto
paras: The Maple Leafs have won two in a row, and the Flyers (10-12-6) beat Vancouver 5-2 on Friday. Going in, the Flyers are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Leafs last in the Atlantic (tied for 25th).

The Flyers’ record (.464) is about what their chances are worth. The Maple Leafs have played better than their record (.426) says: their chances are worth about .493, mostly because they’re 3-10 in one-goal games.

The Flyers play slow, tight games (2nd lowest), take away shots from the point (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). As for the Maple Leafs, they take a lot of low-quality shots (31st) and take more penalties than they draw (30th). They also get their shots through better than anyone (1st), and their knack for getting shots through meets the Flyers’ shot blockers. The Flyers have the edge over the Maple Leafs on depth.

Matvei Michkov (11 G / 9 A / 20 P in 27 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Christian Dvorak (5 G / 12 A / 17 P in 28 GP) isn’t far behind. Auston Matthews (14 G / 20 A / 34 P in 27 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with six goals in nine games against Philadelphia since 2023-24. William Nylander (11 G / 14 A / 25 P in 27 GP) isn’t far behind.

Anthony Stolarz (7-5-1 / .907 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Toronto. Philadelphia has two options in net: Dan Vladař (5-5-4 / .875 SV% in 14 GS) and Joseph Woll (5-7-2 / .886 SV% in 14 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Vladař got the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Jim Hiller likes to send McKenna, Sissons and Tavares out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Bunting, Cates and Martone.

items.text: Simon Benoit faces Toronto for the first time since leaving.
John Tavares has a point in seven straight games against Philadelphia, and 14 points in his last nine against them.
The Flyers are newly without Owen Tippett.

The Maple Leafs are newly without Chris Tanev and Jack Roslovic, and have been without Nick Blankenburg since Oct 22. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Avalanche are missing more right now.
